prose: Ed Zitron's 7,000-word premium essay 'How Much Money Does AI Need?' opens with a meta-apology for its length - specificity is his method - and then takes aim at AI boosterism's relationship with numbers: hundreds of billions and trillions get declared, and the boosters assume nobody would say such things in bad faith and that the industry will certainly deliver.

His anchor point: we're barely a few years from Mark Zuckerberg burning $80 billion on the metaverse - 'what will one day be known as the second-worst misallocation of capital', with the implication of what the first-worst will be. (Summary based on the free opening section; the full essay is paywalled.)
highlights: Zitron's question: how much money does AI actually need - and who checked?
Boosters treat hundred-billion-dollar declarations as inherently good-faith
The metaverse's $80B burn is his calibration point for capital misallocation
A 7,000-word premium essay; summary based on the free opening
He defends length as method: specificity over soundbite
